notes.body:
**35 new Water cards for the Base Set** - twelve Summons, eight Spells and a Wizard who counters, nine permanents and Traps, and five Treasures (one of them the first **Treasure Building**) - with the designer's art. The computer plays every one of them. Also: **damage that isn't "direct" now meets Defense** (Heat Blink Garuda and eleven more), the computer's Frostmane goes for your Guardian, no freeze on a Draft fight's finishing blow, nothing attacks a fallen Guardian, and the game remembers fullscreen.

### Summons

- **Archerfish Corsair** (Common) - a Fish Pirate that shoots from range. [1], [A]: draw a card; unless you have more cards in your Treasure Chest than your opponent, put a card from your hand back on top of your deck.
- **Crush Claw Crab** (Common) - moves only diagonally, one diagonal step for 1 Movement. [1 Water]: switch its Attack with its Defense until the end of turn - a 4-Attack crab becomes a 4-Defense wall on your opponent's turn.
- **Giant Angler Fish** (Common) - a 6/6 Water Breather that has Diving while you have a Trap set.
- **Inkspray Squid** (Common) - Manifest: deactivate and deplete any permanent, a Summon, a Worker or even a Building, whose [A] then waits for its next Active Phase.
- **Sea Giant** (Uncommon) - Skyscraper; Manifest: draw two cards.
- **Slippery Elemental** (Uncommon) - a 1-cost body nothing can attack, not even a Guardian. Spells still reach it, and Hammer and Anvil still gets at it.
- **Zishin Pupil** (Common, [1 Water]) - a young Wizard whose Summon Spell, **Recite** [1 Mana], draws you a card.
- **Siren Watcher** (Uncommon, [1][1 Water]) - a Guardprotect Siren; tap it to regenerate 1 Life.
- **Bull Shark** (Rare, [4][1 Water]) - Water Breather, Diving, Attack 3, Life 4. At the start of your End Phase, if any Summon perished this turn, it grows +1A/+1 max Life for good.
- **Pistol Shrimp** (Rare, [2][1 Water]) - Ranged Combat 2. Every Spell you cast from your hand lets it shoot one field further until the end of turn (a Summon's own Summon Spell is cast by the Summon, not by you, so it does not count).
- **Seastar** (Rare, [3][1 Water]) - a Guardprotect wall with Life 6 that never moves. Your Water Incantations cost [1] less for each Seastar you have.
- **Silverfin School** (Rare, [1][2 Water]) - Water Breather. Whenever it deals combat damage - attacking or striking back - you draw that many cards.

### Counters and Spells

- **Second Guess** - [1 Water], Quick: negate an Incantation unless its controller pays [1]. The player whose card it is gets the question "Pay [1], or it is negated?" - and if they cannot pay, it is simply negated.
- **Even Exchange** - Quick: negate an Incantation; then each player draws a card.
- **Douse** - Quick: negate an Earth or Fire Incantation.
- **Seasoned Wizard** - a Human Wizard whose Summon Spell **Stay the Hand** is Quick: on your opponent's turn, or in answer to a card on the Stack, select her and press her button to negate their Incantation unless they pay [2].
- **Catalogue** - Quick: draw three, then put a card from your hand on top or on the bottom of your deck.
- **Soothing Waters** - either Guardian gains 3 life.
- **Still or Stir** - choose: deactivate and deplete two Summons, or reactivate two; then draw a card. It names its two Summons as it resolves, and a Summon no Spell of yours could target (a Shadow Veil, Signet of the Lion Order, one in Clear Lake already targeted this turn) is not one it can name; naming one in Clear Lake uses up its one targeting that turn.
- **Fishing for More** - shuffle a card from your hand into your deck to draw a card from your Treasure Chest.
- **Always a Bigger Fish** - sacrifice a Summon; the first Summon in your deck that costs more comes straight into your Guarded Zone.

### Permanents and Traps

- **Led Astray** (Enchantment): enchant a Summon standing on your side of the board - an enemy that walked in - and it is yours for as long as Led Astray stays on it, wherever it goes.
- **Open Secrets** (Rune): draw a card; while it is in play your opponent plays with their hand face up on your screen.
- **Swim with the Fishes** (Curse, 2 turns): every Summon the cursed player controls has Water Breather - pay [2] or [1 Water] for each in their Guardian Phase, or lose it (a Sea Terrain still saves them).
- **Clear Lake** (Terrain - Lake): your Summons in it regenerate 2 Life as it arrives, and each of them can be targeted by Spells and abilities only once a turn.
- **Shark Tooth** (Equipment): +1A and +1 Movement in an aquatic Terrain; sacrifice it to search your deck for a big Water Summon.
- **Arcane Forge** (Building): once a turn, a Spell you cast finds you another Spell of the same cost; sacrifice it to shuffle your spent Spells back and draw two.
- **Whirlpool**, **Sea Toll** and **Copy Homework** (Traps): make a Summon that wanders in pay its cost again or sink to the bottom of the deck; draw cards equal to its cost; copy an opponent's Spell by finding one of the same cost in your deck.

### Treasures

- **Akuari War Horn** (Treasure Item - Artifact): calls a 3/3 **Trident Warrior** (Nix, Warrior, range 2) into your Guarded Zone as it enters, and another every Tactic Phase you pay [3][1 Water] and tap it. Each time one of your Nix slays an enemy Summon, your Guardian gains 1 life.
- **Curse of Echoes** (Treasure Spell - Curse, forever): whenever the cursed player draws outside their own Draw Phase - Treasure Chest draws included - you may draw a card.
- **Encryption Dragon** (Treasure Summon): its Manifest finds a Spell with cost 4 or less in your deck and sends it into the Void, **encrypted**. Its Summon Spell **Crack the Code** [1 Mana] puts a copy of that Spell in your hand: cast it as usual, paying its cost (it is gone at the end of the turn if you don't). Each Dragon cracks only its own code.
- **Marid's Dream** (Treasure): find a Spell in your deck, show it, shuffle, and put it on top.
- **Merchant Harbor** - the first **Treasure Building**: discard a Worker card and pay [1] to draw, or return a Worker to your hand and pay [1] to negate a Spell unless its controller pays [2]. Neither taps it, so it can do either as often as you can pay. Life 4, Defense 1.

### Changed

- **Academy Professor's Deny** now asks its target's controller whether they pay [2], instead of paying it for them whenever they could.
- The computer answers your Incantations with its Seasoned Wizard and Academy Professor, and casts a "pay or it is negated" counter only when you cannot pay.
- **One "pay or it is negated" question** for every soft counter: Second Guess, Seasoned Wizard's Stay the Hand, Academy Professor's Deny and Merchant Harbor all ask it the same way, with their own price.

### Plain damage meets Defense
- **Heat Blink Garuda's Demise no longer ignores Defense.** "Deal 2 damage to each Summon" now meets each Summon's Defense like any hit: a Defense 1 Summon loses 1 Life, not 2. The rule behind it (your ruling of 2026-11-22): only damage a card calls **direct** goes past Defense and Resistance; every other "deals N damage" is a normal hit.
- **Eleven more cards, and the Burned ailment, dealt direct damage their text never printed.** Each one now meets Defense (shown here against a Defense 1 Summon):

| Card | Printed words | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Heat Blink Garuda | "Demise - Deal 2 damage to each Summon." | 2 to Life | 1 to Life |
| Crazed Charge Goblin | "Demise - ... deals 2 damage to each Summon in this zone and each adjacent zone." | 2 | 1 |
| Firebelly Goblin (token) | "Demise - This Summon deals 1 damage to up to one target Guardian or Summon." | 1 | 0 (a Guardian still takes 1) |
| Phoenix Flame Shaman | "Demise - This Summon deals X damage to target permanent, where X was its maximum life." | X | X - 1 |
| Hoarding Wyrm | "Demise - Deal 4 damage to target Summon." | 4 | 3 |
| Tormenter | "Infiltrate - This Summon deals 1 damage to target permanent or Guardian." | 1 | 0 (a Guardian still takes 1) |
| Smoldering Infiltrator | "Infiltrate - This Summon deals 2 damage to target Summon. If this damage does not deal direct damage, the attacked Summon becomes burned." | 2, and Burned whenever it lived | 1, and Burned only when Defense stops all 2 (so a Defense 2 Summon is Burned, one that loses Life is not) |
| Burned (the ailment it gives) | "During the guardian phase of its controller, this summon takes 1 damage." | 1 every Guardian Phase | the first tick wears Defense, and since a Burned Summon's Defense does not come back, every tick after reaches Life |
| Frost Burn | "At the end of each turn, Frost Burn deals 1 damage to each Frozen Summon." | 1 | 0 |
| Big Storm | "At the end of each turn, Big Storm deals 1 damage to each non-Wind Summon in the affected zone." | 1 | 0 |
| Burning Crater | "Burning Crater deals 4 damage to the activating Summon and 1 damage to its controller's Guardian." | 4 | 3 (the Guardian still takes 1) |
| Backdraft | "Backdraft deals 3 damage to the activating Summon. ..." | 3 | 2 |
| Advanced Pyromancy | "Advanced Pyromancy deals X damage to target permanent, where X is equal to the Magic of target Summon you control. ..." | X | X - 1, and it now gets what adds to a Spell's damage (Pyromaniac, Bolt Hill), as other damage Spells do |

- **Left as they were, on purpose:** every card that prints "direct damage" (Fire Wall, Ice Spikes, Frost Ray, Bone Archer, Scorching Red Dragon, Spike Coil Thrasher, Youthful Archer, Intrusive Thought's first mode, Nest of Vipers, Smogpit Warrens, War-Cry of the Scarred, Quake, Barbed Bomb's 1 to the others, Flashfire's 2 to the activating Summon, Powderkeg Goblin, Goblin Catapult's shot, Rain of Fire, Raging Fires, Ifrit's Lamp, Gloom Demon, Moryrak, Firebrand Barracks, Cinder Watch, Thorn Trap, Jungle Trap, Impale, Kiwtryn's Legacy, Grinding Strata's Enhance, Thornwood Reserve, Burn Out); Burning Footsteps' Fire Brand ("takes 1 direct damage"); Flaming Kirin (your ruling of 2026-08-30 that it is direct); and every "loses N life" (Poison, Forgotten Wraith), which is not damage at all.
- **Side effects:** the fixed cards no longer count for Flaming Minds ("direct damage dealt") or set off Bleeding Wounds ("takes direct damage") - they deal plain damage now, as a plain-damage Spell already did. The computer's Demise picks (Phoenix Flame Shaman, Hoarding Wyrm, Firebelly Goblin, Sootgut Bombardier) count a kill only if the damage gets past the target's Defense.
- **The log shows Defense at work.** When one of these cards hits a Summon that lives, its line now says how much Defense kept off - "Heat Blink Garuda's Demise: 2 damage to Bare, Shield (mitigated 1)." - as an attack's line already did.
- **Kindlemaster**'s +1 now joins the hit before Defense: under a Kindlemaster a Burning tick deals 2, and a Defense 1 Summon still loses 1 (it used to be added only to what got past Defense).

### Fixed
- **The computer's Frostmane now attacks your Guardian.** It was played as a pure wall: it held its own side of the board, so it never stood in your Guarded Zone, where a Summon attacks a Guardian from. Now it still guards and still never takes on a Summon it cannot kill, but it walks into your Guarded Zone and swings at your Guardian when that is safe - not while its own Guardian is in danger, not where one of your Summons or your Guardian could kill it there, and not behind a Guardprotect body; if it ever has nothing to do there, it walks back out. Snow Covered Mimic and Immovable Sentinel stay at home as before.
- **No more freeze on a Draft fight's finishing blow.** When a Draft fight ended, the game drafted your next opponent's whole deck there and then, in the frame of the blow - the screen stood still for about two thirds of a second before the result came up (0.67 s in `tools/b1029_draft_end_probe`; the longest frame 0.72 s). The opponent is now drafted in the background while the fight is being played, and the draft itself is about seven times quicker (it looked every card up by walking the whole pool of 2,000). The end of the fight now takes 3 ms, like any other game's end. It is the same opponent it would have been: a run plays out exactly as before.
- **A fallen Guardian can't be attacked any more.** In a Draft game your Brave Bonded Knight attacked the computer's Guardian after "Orsonius wins!" - an attack still on its way when the Guardian fell went through, and so did a click in the very frame of the finishing blow. Once a Guardian has fallen nothing attacks or moves - an attack on its way to a Summon or a Building stops too.
- **The game remembers fullscreen.** It always opened as a 1920x1080 window, so fullscreen had to be switched on again after every launch; the choice is now kept in your profile (and picking a window size from the list goes back to a window). Tools and test runs never change it.
- A Summon given Diving by a card (Nix Lord, Spontaneous Gills, the Angler Fish) now shows the Diving badge on the board.
- A Summon sent to the bottom or top of a deck (Whirlpool, and the older cards that do it) no longer leaves a stray "returns to its owner's hand" line in the log.
- Cards that say "Switch this Summon's Attack..." or "Switch target Summon's..." (Windshifter, Dishevel, Reversed Polarity) no longer explain the Switch Movement Ability in their details.

### Fixed
- **Creeping Granite** now does what it prints. The two Treasures it takes are **paid for** - with [Earth] paying any colour - where until now they were cast for nothing; the player whose draw set it off **no longer keeps that card** ("Instead": it goes back and is one of the two taken); and a taken card that is played still goes to its owner's graveyard when it leaves play.

### Fixed
- **Bot Match's deck screen was slow** - every click on a deck or an opponent took seconds, and opening the screen longer still. Build 1025's "Not playable" check on the opponent tiles read every saved deck from disk again for each of the 112 tiles. The decks are now read once when the screen opens: a click takes about a tenth of a second (`tools/b1026_botmatch_lag_probe`: 6.4 s before, 0.09 s now).

**Garl's Gabl is once per turn**, and his question tells the truth under a Three-Headed Dragon.

### Changed
- **Garl, Guardian of Fire** - "Once per turn, whenever a source you control deals 3 or more damage ...". With a Three-Headed Dragon out, every 3 Garl dealt set him off again; a hit you turn down also uses the turn's one.
- **Flood of Thought** has no Resonance tag any more. It works as before.

### Fixed
- Under a Three-Headed Dragon, Garl asked "deal 1 damage to it, and 1 damage to himself?" and logged 1 while 3 and 3 landed. The question and the log now show the real numbers.
- Turning Garl down logged "<Guardian> stays in the graveyard."; it now says Garl does nothing.
- The Goblin Catapult's log said it "takes 1 damage and falls apart" when a Three-Headed Dragon had made it 3.

**25 new Treasures for the Base Set** - five Darkness, five Fire, five Light and ten Neutral - with the designer's art. Draw them from your Treasure Chest as usual; the computer plays every one of them. Also: **Shift+click** in the Deck Builder, a deck needs a **full Treasure Chest** to be played, and fixes for dragging a Spell onto a Guardian, Dragon Heart's pump and the sprung-Trap label.

### Darkness

- **Absolute Darkness** ([1 Darkness], a Ritual, Preparation Time 2): while it prepares, **no combat damage is dealt at all** - not by your Summons, not by theirs, not to a Guardian. When it finishes you look at the top cards of your deck - as many as your Guardian is short of 15 Life - and keep one; the rest go to the bottom in a random order. The lower you are, the deeper you dig.
- **Chains of the Underworld** ([1][1 Darkness], a Curse that never ends): the cursed player skips their Draw Phase and draws at the beginning of their End Phase instead - a card a turn late, and right before the hand limit.
- **Corpse Strings** ([2][1 Darkness]): the Summon nearest the top of your graveyard comes back onto a free field of your Guarded Zone that you choose. Then, if you hold fewer cards than your Treasure Chest does, Corpse Strings goes back to the bottom of your Chest to be drawn again.
- **Dragon of Rot** ([3][2 Darkness], 6 Life, 4A/4M, Dual Combat R2): whenever any Summon dies - yours, theirs, or the Dragon itself - its controller's Guardian loses 1 life.
- **Soul of the Lich** ([4 Darkness], a Curse that never ends - usually on yourself): you **don't lose while your Guardian is at 0 or less**. But every heal hurts you instead, every Summon of yours that dies "heals" you for 2 (so it hurts for 2), and every time your Guardian loses life the Curse gets a Doom Counter. At six it is sacrificed - and if you are at 0 or less then, you lose.

### Fire

- **Barbarian Mustering** ([1 Fire]): as you cast it, sacrifice up to five Fire Workers; a Barbarian token (1 Life, 2 Attack) appears for each, on Guarded Zone fields you pick. Then **all your Summons get +1A and Zealing** this turn - the Barbarians too, so they swing at once.
- **Curse of the Tinderbox** ([2][2 Fire], Duration 3): whenever a Summon enters on the cursed player's side, each of their other Summons takes 1 damage. If they play no Summon in a turn, the Curse lasts a turn longer.
- **Hammer and Anvil** ([2 Fire], a Rune): pin an enemy between two of your Summons. A Summon of yours attacking an enemy that stands next to another Summon of yours gets **+1A** and can attack it **even if something says it can't be attacked** - Flying, Shadow Veil, a "can't be attacked" effect. Only Grace still protects it.
- **Raging Fires** ([1][2 Fire]): choose your half of the board or theirs - 3 direct damage to every Summon standing there, whoever owns it. The two fast-lane fields belong to both halves, so they burn either way.
- **Three-Headed Dragon** ([3][3 Fire], 5 Life, 3A/3M, Dual Combat R1, no Flying): **anything you control that would deal 1 or 2 damage deals 3 instead** - attacks, Spells, abilities, a Guardian hit. Defense still counts after: a 1-Attack Summon hitting Defense 1 deals 2.

### Light

- **Alms Bowl** ([3][1 Light], Artifact). At the beginning of your End Phase your Guardian gains 1 life. Click it in your Permanents box and choose: **[A]** - each of your Summons regenerates 1 Life; or **[2][2 Light], [A], sacrifice it** - pick a non-Treasure permanent card in your graveyard and take it back to your hand.
- **Comrade-in-Arms** ([2 Light], Life 3, Attack 2, Defense 1, Bi Combat R2). The second time your Summons attack in a turn, you draw a card.
- **Curse of Nonviolence** ([2][1 Light], Duration 2). Pick a player: they can't declare attacks - not with their Summons, not with their Guardian - until it runs out.
- **Divine Intervention** (Positionless Trap, [2][1 Light] to activate). When your Guardian would fall to 0 Life, the game stops and asks you. Activate it and your Guardian stays at 1; until your next Active Phase its Life can't go below 1, you and your Guardian can't be targeted by Spells or abilities, and all damage to your permanents is prevented. You draw a card, too.
- **Hour of Triumph** ([3][2 Light]). Pick a free field of your Guarded Zone and an enemy Summon with cost 3 or more: a Soldier token appears, every Summon you control gains +1A/+1D/+1M/+1R and +1 max Life for good, and the enemy is destroyed.

### Neutral

- **Sword of Legends** ([4], Weapon, Durability 3). While it is in play, no Summon can regenerate Life. The equipped Summon gets +1A for each Equipment you control (the Sword counts), and +1A more for each of Mask of Legends and Shield of Legends you control.
- **Shield of Legends** ([4], Armor, Durability 3). Your Equipment can't be destroyed by Spells, abilities or effects (it still breaks when its Durability runs out). Once per turn, all damage to the equipped Summon is prevented.
- **Mask of Legends** ([3], Accessory, Durability 3). +2D/+2R. At the beginning of your End Phase, if you have all three Legends and no Legendary Hero, you pick a field in your Guarded Zone: a **Legendary Hero** (Life 4, Attack 2, Defense 1, Resistance 1) appears there and puts on all three - for free, no Durability spent.
- **Book of Arcane Wisdom** ([2], Artifact): its **[A]** puts a Wisdom Counter on it. Click its tile once it has counters and choose **"Remove X"**: then pick an Incantation from your hand that costs X or less - you cast it for free, right away (or later this turn).
- **Convergence** ([6], Artifact): whenever you cast an Incantation, every Incantation of a **different card type** costs [2] less this turn. Cast a Summon, and your Spells, Items, Buildings and Terrains are cheaper; cast a Spell too, and your Items are [4] cheaper.
- **Eternal Cycle** ([5], Rune): at the beginning of each End Phase, every card (except Treasures) that went to a graveyard this turn goes to the bottom of its owner's deck. Nothing stays dead for long.
- **Iron Ceiling** ([2], Rune): no player can cast an Incantation that costs more than the Workers they control. An X counts at the X you choose.
- **Mercury Golem** ([1], Golem, Dual Combat R1): costs [1] more for every Summon on the board - and as it lands it gains +1A/+1M/+1 max Life for every Summon on the board, itself included.
- **Mirror of Nothingness** ([1], Artifact): no player can cast an Incantation with the same name as a permanent already in play (Workers excepted).
- **Taxing Leech** ([3], 3/3 Leech): Incantations and activated abilities that cost 1 or 2 Energy cost [2] more - for both players, you too. A [1][1 Fire] card costs [3][1 Fire]; an [A] with no Energy cost stays free.

### The Deck Builder and playable decks

#### New
- **Shift+click in the Deck Builder puts the maximum in or takes it all out.** Shift+click a card in the grid to add every copy its limit still allows (in the Main Deck, or in the Sideboard while that tab is open - they share the limit). A Worker with no limit goes in **4 at a time**. A Treasure, or a card banked into the chest from the Treasures tab, goes in once as always. Shift+click a row of your deck list to take every copy of that card out. The hint over a card and the row's tooltip say so.

#### Changed
- **A deck without a full Treasure Chest can't be played any more.** The chest needs its 5 cards (4 under Taitor), at least 4 of them Treasures (one non-Treasure, two under Morel) and no card twice. Such a deck now shows **"Not playable"** with the reason on Bot Match (as your deck, and as the opponent - one of your own decks in hot-seat) and in the CPU Tournament's pick, Play stays off with the reason under it, and the Deck Builder's **Play vs computer** says why instead of starting. In the Deck Builder the Treasures tab's count turns amber while the chest is not right, and its tooltip says what is missing. A Main Deck under 55 still plays against the computer, as before; online still asks for a deck legal in the match's Format. Every shipped deck is playable; Draft, Dungeon and Campaign decks are not affected.

#### Fixed
- In the Deck Builder's Treasures tab, a card already in the chest can no longer be banked a second time (under Morel's two non-Treasure slots it could).

### In a match

#### Fixed
- **Drag a Spell onto a Guardian and it is cast.** Searing Slag (or any Spell that can hit a Guardian) let go on the Guardian's portrait used to say "Choose a target" and stay in your hand - only a click worked. Now the drop casts it, and your open Workers pay for it as they do for a click. Too short even with the Workers, it stays in your hand and you can drag it again. And a Spell your open Workers will pay for no longer says "Not enough Energy" while you hold it - the line now says the Workers will pay.
- **Dragon Heart's pump on a Summon that has its own ability or Summon Spell.** On Soul Scorch Ifrit the button said "Cast Spell", and on Flame Guard or the Ifrit picking Dragon Heart's [1][1 Fire] actually used the Summon's own ability instead. The button now says "Activate Ability", the choice names Dragon Heart's pump, and picking it gives +1A/+1M. And when neither ability can be used right now (the Ifrit at equal Life, no Energy for the pump), "Cast Spell" casts Cursed Wish again - it used to do nothing at all. The computer was caught by the same thing: it could spend its whole turn trying to cast that Spell.

#### Changed
- **Who sprang a Trap, in plain words.** The tag on the Summon that set a Trap off said "Set it off", which read like an order, and said it on the enemy's Traps too. It now says **"Sprang your Trap"** or **"Sprang their Trap"**, and the line under the Trap says **"Your Trap - sprung by the opponent's Walker"** or **"Their Trap - sprung by your Stepper"**. Online, each player reads it from their own side.

### Fixed

- **A Summon cast while a "whenever you cast" trigger goes on the Stack above it** (Convergence; Valuables Pest's when the Summon is a Treasure) gets its Manifest **once** - it fired twice (Scout Hound drew two cards).
- **Denial by Light**'s +2 Life now goes through the ordinary life-gain road, so the effects that change a gain (Soul of the Lich, the lockouts) see it.

### Changed

- **No Rune prints "Perpetual" any more** (the designer: "Yes, all runes drop it"). A Rune's lines are always on by its type. The last four lose the word from their text and their keywords: **Fractured Reflex**, **Rune of Penance**, **Sol's Decree**, and **Heat of Battle** (keyword only - its text never printed it). Nothing they do changes; three faces re-rendered.

**Fire's Base Set is in: 29 new cards** with the designer's art, and the computer plays all of them. Funeral Toll now asks before it pays.

### Changed

- **Red Incineration Dragon:** Life 8 -> 6 and limit 4 -> 3. Its **[X][X][1 Fire]** shot now reads "target Building or Summon" and really hits a Building: press the ability, pick X, then click the enemy Building's tile. A Building takes it on its Defense first. The computer now uses the shot too - for a kill on your priciest Summon or Building it can pay for - and then it still attacks with the Dragon that turn.
- **Bloodhungry Frenzy** has no Frenzy any more - you control the Summon again. It still gives **+2A/+1 Movement**, and now: **at the beginning of your End Phase, if the Summon could have moved but didn't, or could have attacked but didn't, it loses 1 life.** Move it and swing with it every turn you can.
- **Focused Hit** costs **[1][1 Fire]** (was [1 Fire]) and is Common now.
- **Sabotage** reads "Destroy target Summon, Worker or Item" - the same card, cleaner wording (Buildings are not part of it).

### Summons and the Goblin Catapult

- **Tiger Beetle** (1, Zealing) attacks the turn it lands. **Goblin Foot Soldier** is Fire's honest 2-drop. **War-Crazed Minotaur** hits with Swiftstrike, **Dragon Hatchling** flies for 3, and **Emberwing Drake**, a 4/4 flier for 5, can move the turn it enters.
- **Perentie Blitzer** (2, Zealing, range 2) raids and runs: at the end of your turn, if it moved or attacked, you put it on a free field of your Guarded Zone. You pick the field; with no free field it stays where it is.
- **Firebelly Fanatic** (1) - when it dies, it deals 1 damage to any target: click a Summon, or a Guardian's portrait.
- **Flame Guard** (3) is a Guardprotect wall with 5 Life and Magic 0 - and **[1 Fire]: +1M until the end of turn**, any number of times, on your opponent's turn too. Pump it when it is attacked and it hits back with what you paid for.
- **Cannonball Goblin** (2) - **[1]: +1A and Flying until the end of turn**, once a turn; at the next End Phase it is sacrificed, and when it dies it deals 1 damage to each Guardian, yours too.
- **Blaze Elemental** (6) - when it dies, 3 magic damage to every Summon on the board, yours included.
- **Bloodcraving Mercenary** (2, a 3/3 with range 2) can only be cast once a permanent or a Guardian has lost Life this turn. Damage that only wears down Defense doesn't count. Until then the card doesn't glow, and clicking it tells you why.
- **Soul Scorch Ifrit** (5) - **[1]: Flying until the end of turn**, only while your Guardian has less Life than your opponent's. Its Summon Spell **Cursed Wish** (2 Mana) deals 2 damage to your own Guardian, then you look at your top three cards: one into your hand, the other two into your graveyard.
- **Goblin Catapult** (a Building, 3) - you may **sacrifice a Goblin instead of returning its two Workers**: casting it asks "Return 2 Workers" or "Sacrifice <your Goblin>". **[A]: 1 direct damage to any target, and 1 damage to itself**. Three shots and it falls apart.
- **The computer** plays them too. It fires its Catapult every turn (a kill if a Summon is at 1 Life, otherwise your Guardian) and pays for one with a Goblin when it is short of Workers. It launches the Cannonball only for a kill or the game, and pumps its Flame Guard when one pump makes the counterattack kill your attacker. It casts Cursed Wish while its Guardian can spare the Life.
- **Sounds:** the Goblins, the Minotaur, the two Dragons and the Beetle arrive with theirs; the two Fire Elementals and the Ifrit arrive in a burst of fire, and the Mercenary - a woman - with her voice.
- The Glimmer Fairy's "carried back to the Guarded Zone" line now names whatever moved the Summon (Delta Coilhold, Perentie Blitzer), not always the Fairy.

### Spells and Items

### Fixed

- **Funeral Toll asks before it pays.** When an enemy Summon slays one of yours, Funeral Toll goes on the Stack and you get a question: "Pay [1]?" - then you choose what loses the 1 life. Before, the only sign was a glow on the board, and clicking any Summon - to look at it, say - paid the toll on it. Anything else waiting on the Stack (an Onslaught from the same attack) now waits for your answer.
- **Discounts on Items now apply when you cast them.** Siege Foundry's [1] off Equipment, Eternal Fall Hime's off Nature Items, Evora's, and Ocean Wave Seashell's on a Water Item showed on the card but the cast still asked the full price (the Seashell's discount was even used up). Now the price on the card is what you pay - Dragon Heart's discount too.

### Stack triggers

**A trigger on the Stack is its card, drawn live.** A Manifest, Demise, Resonance, Onslaught, Infiltrate, Assault or Agility used to pop up on an old cut-out frame - the name and a bare "Summon" typed over it, the clause in plain text with no keyword colours, and a round badge covering the right of the text box (only five elements even had that frame). Now it is the card's own face, the way it looks in your hand: its full type line ("Summon - Demon - Darkness"), its element's frame, a Treasure's frame, and in the text box only the trigger that is happening, headed by its keyword in that keyword's colours - "**Manifest** - Each player discards a card ...", "**Agility** - Leave a Fire Brand ...". Every element, Wind included.

- **A trigger a card was given** shows the line from whatever gave it - Agatha wearing Gale-Edge Sabre shows "**Assault** - If the equipped Summon moved this turn ...", not her own abilities. A keyword given with no words to show is just the keyword.
- **A card whose whole text is the trigger** (Smoldering Strider) shows its printed face.
- **The turn timer's fuse and its "Answer 7" no longer draw across the card** being shown on the Stack: the Stack's cards are on top.
- **Only the trigger's own lines.** A trigger used to run on into the lines after it - Outpost Quartermaster's Manifest showed its two [A] abilities too, Blessed Spy's Infiltrate its Block. It now stops at the card's next ability (a "Choose one:" keeps its options).
- **Answering a question against the clock:** while a question is open (a discard asked by your opponent's card, say), the fuse and "Answer 7" run along the top of the screen above it, instead of hiding under its dark shade.
- Online, the other player sees the same.

### Who set off the Trap, and the Standard

- **You can see who set off a Trap.** When a Trap springs - yours or your opponent's, a Step, Zone, Universal or Positionless Trap - the Summon that set it off wears a pulsing amber ring and a "Set it off" tag while the Trap card is shown, and a line under the card names it: "Set off by the opponent's Walker", "Set off by your Stepper". When an attack set it off (Failed Exploration, Deathless Pact, Heated Riposte...), it names the attacker - "Set off by an attack from the opponent's Slayer" - and an amber arrow runs to it, even though the Trap itself protects your defender. Online, both players see the same Summon marked, each told from their own side.
- **The Trap window names it too**, before you decide: "... Set off by the opponent's Walker."
- It never gives away a hidden card: Doom Long Lost's window says "Set off by the opponent", not the card they just drew from their Chest. And when the attacker that set off your Trap is killed first (by another Trap of the same attack), it still names that attacker, never your own defender.
- **Standard for the Fallen** (checked, nothing to fix): its [A] goes on the Stack and waits there, shown in the Stack, while your opponent can answer; when they have nothing that could answer, it resolves right after it is shown, as every ability does. The computer does not use the Standard's [A] yet.

- **Foxkin Glory-Seeker** dies with a woman's voice.
